title: Lamport Logical Timestamp Synchronization Engine in php: Causal Clock Verification and Execution Dynamics
description: Lamport logical clocks are a cornerstone for establishing causal order in distributed systems, yet practical implementations in high-level scripting language...
abstract: Lamport logical clocks are a cornerstone for establishing causal order in distributed systems, yet practical implementations in high-level scripting languages remain under-explored. This paper presents a PHP-based Lamport Logical Timestamp Synchronization Engine that integrates a height-balanced search index for event logging. We formalize three research questions concerning (RQ1) the asymptotic complexity of timestamp-driven insertions, (RQ2) the preservation of a strict monotonicity invariant across remote updates, and (RQ3) the empirical throughput and latency profile on a modern multi-core workstation. The engine is built from verified source files (engine.php, types.php, main.php) and evaluated over 30 benchmark iterations on a 13th Gen Intel Core i9-13900HX (24 cores/32 threads, 63.8~GB RAM, Windows 11). Measured mean latency is 60 300.89 \textmu{}s with a throughput of 16 584 ops/s. Results confirm that the balanced index maintains $O(\log n)$ insertion cost while respecting Lamport's causal ordering. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261011_094516_lamport_logical_timestamp_sync}.
